title: Embedding RankInspector: per-path telemetry, cost attribution, and trace playbook
creator: Lydia Chen
description: Build a consolidated observability surface (RankInspector) for embeddings + reranking endpoints that surfaces: per-route latency distributions, per-request trace spans, token / GPU cost attribution, and actionable alerts. Deliverables: dashboards, trace conventions, cost breakdown pipeline, runbook snippets, and a phased rollout for high-cardinality routes.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route dashboard that shows 95th/99th latency, median latency, QPS, error rate, and tokens per request for embeddings and rerank endpoints
Trace span spec and instrumentation merged to runtime repo with < 1% added p50 latency overhead in synthetic load test
Cost attribution pipeline computes per-route token and GPU-second cost daily and exposes a per-route metric in telemetry store
Alerting rules for latency SLO breaches and unexpected cost increases with annotated runbook links
Migration plan for high-cardinality route tags to safe low-cardinality route_key mapping
work_notes: 2026-03-02: Kickoff sync with PM and Observability team. Agreed to use existing metrics namespace 'redwood.emb.rankinspector' to avoid proliferation.
2026-03-04: Prototype trace spans in local runtime. Added spans: input-embed, embedding-batch, vector-score, rerank-merge. Observed 0.6% median increase in empty-run synthetic test.
2026-03-06: Design review with Console team: dashboard layout approved, recommended single-pane latency cost combo with route filter and sampling toggle.
2026-03-08: Implemented sampling filter to limit traces to 1% by default, 10% for routes with active QA label. Need product decision for increasing sampling on canary.
2026-03-09: PR opened in github.com/redwood/runtime #8621 for span instrumentation and metric tags. Linked below.
decisions: Use deterministic route_key mapping: hash(normalized_route) => route_key to keep cardinality under 10k for telemetry store
Cost model will attribute GPU-second proportional to token-generation time using existing runtime token timers; perfect-per-token accuracy deferred to ENG-41875
Default trace sampling set to 1% across hosted routes, 5% for Dedicated customers with debug mode enabled
Tagging policy: include route_key, model_family, quantization_profile, and customer_tier as low-cardinality tags only
telemetry_plan: Emit new metrics under redwood.emb.rankinspector: route_qps, route_95_latency_ms, route_99_latency_ms, route_median_latency_ms, route_error_rate, route_tokens_per_request, route_gpu_seconds. Augment traces with span attributes: route_key, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, quant_profile. Ship daily aggregated cost file to billing pipeline and expose route_cost_per_24h metric.
dashboard_widgets: Top-level: heatmap of route 95th latency by model_family over time
Route table: sortable list of route_key with QPS, median latency, p95 latency, error rate, tokens/request, daily cost
Trace sampler panel: recent sampled traces list with expandable spans and tag filters
Cost trend: 7/30 day change in GPU-seconds and token consumption per route
SLO pulse: % of routes meeting p95 < 300ms with quick links to associated traces
alert_rules: Latency SLO breach: if route_99_latency_ms > 5x baseline for 10m => pager to infra-team; runbook link included
Cost spike: route_cost_per_24h increases > 200% week-over-week and absolute cost > $50/day for the route => create ticket and notify owner
Error surge: route_error_rate > 2% for 5m and increases by > 3x relative to trailing hour => paging with trace links
Trace backlog: if sampled traces ingestion lag > 5m, open infra alert to tracing pipeline team
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary 10 routes): enable detailed spans + cost tagging for 10 low-traffic routes and validate metrics for 48h. Phase 2 (beta 200 routes): expand route_key mapping and dashboards; increase trace sampling to 2% for beta. Phase 3 (global): enable aggregated metrics for all routes with default 1% sampling. Provide opt-out per-customer for privacy/compliance.
open_questions: Should we surface per-request token cost to end customers in usage UI or keep it internal to the billing pipeline? (Need PM decision)
What is the acceptable maximum telemetry cardinality for our TSDB without impacting query latency? Observability team to advise.
Do we need consent gating for traces containing request metadata for Private deployments? Security to confirm.
test_plan: Synthetic load: run 3x baseline QPS with instrumented spans; assert median latency overhead < 2% and no added errors
Cost attribution verification: replay 7 days of production traffic in staging and validate route_cost_per_24h within 5% of billing simulation
Dashboard QA: verify widgets render for routes with high-cardinality metadata using route_key mapping
Alert firing test: intentionally inject p99 latency spike in staging and confirm alerting pipeline and runbook link resolution
